ambiguous_node_rule.statement: an ambiguous stage-advance invocation is never written: it is recorded in observed.stage_calls with outcome 'ambiguous' (basis 'hidden' | 'unattributable'), sets observed.ambiguous, and is NOT in observed.walk. The judge compares observed.walk only (the scorer reads the marker rows only and never reads observed.ambiguous), so an ambiguous node can never count as matched, and a walk that needs it fails on `walk`.
ambiguous_node_rule.supersedes: amend-2-instrument fix 2 (chained_stage_advance) fallback 'when the JSON cannot be attributed the call's is_error applies' — for stage-advance only. Under amend-2 an unattributable successful call counted its nodes as written; that is exactly defect 2 below. amend-2's text is otherwise untouched.
ambiguous_node_rule.consistency: the two amendments agree wherever the JSON IS visible (per-invocation JSON outcome); they differ only for invocations whose JSON is not visible, where amend-3 is strictly the stricter reading.

loop_variable_target.defect: lib/stage-graph-cell.js read the target only from a literal `--to [a-z-]+` in the argv text, so `--to $n` yielded to:null and the node was dropped; a `for n in ...; do ... --to $n; done` is ONE argv site but several invocations, so only the first literal-less site was seen and none of the iterations were attributed.

transcript_excerpt.result: three `{"allowed":true,"from":"implement","to":"verify",...` records cut by head -c 150; v2 extractor walk ["plan","implement"], true walk plan,implement,verify,code-review,qc-gate

loop_variable_target.change: stageAdvanceInvocations(): loop bodies (`for VAR in LIST; do ... done`) expand to LIST-length invocations in iteration-major order; each invocation's outcome and target come from its own JSON record in the tool_result (`allowed`, `to`, else `stage`), read tolerantly so a record cut by head -c still names them; the argv literal / loop item is only a fallback name. A refused record (allowed:false, exit 3) is not written. A loop of unknown length, or a record count that does not equal the visible-invocation count, makes the invocations ambiguous (defect 2).

The same outcome for any visible invocation whose JSON cannot be attributed (see ambiguous_node_rule).

A classify call whose stdout also holds another JSON object (a chained `stage-advance --to intent &&` record in front of it) therefore returned the stage-advance object (no eligible_max) and the rung was recorded as 'unobserved' although classify printed eligible_max U1.
